entry.title: Show HN: ReadyStack.dev - Bit-for-bit reproducible OSS containers (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: https://readystack.dev If you are like me, coding LLMs made open source more important not less. A few months ago I wanted to see how far I could get using minimal LLM cost (local on two 3090s and one subscription) to automate OSS containers with a build recipe that matched bits. That project ended up as ReadyStack.dev. ReadyStack publishes free Community Edition containers for open-source applications. I designed it to be a low cost image standard that puts provenance as a first order concern. My goal was to see if I could build in trust with my images in a way nobody else had. Use the build recipe and match bits. Each release's build kit includes everything the build needs: upstream source pinned, the OS packages as .debs, the language dependencies, the base images saved by digest, fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. BUILD_OFFLINE.sh rebuilds with the network off, so mirrors dropping old packages don't matter, and VERIFY_OFFLINE.sh checks your digest against ours. We currently have 101 of 101 releases reproducing their published linux/amd64 digest in our clean-room rebuild process, which is just a trust signal, but an important one as we don't have much of if at all. Certainly, not for free. For full disclosure, I built a sister project, ce.rodeo, which grades container images from all publishers, including ReadyStack.dev. Yes, it is a conflict of interest to grade my own images. I publish the measuring criteria and I needed a standard of what existed so I had to create a grading system first. Happy to hear suggestions. I started out to do something for OSS. I designed it to run on a skinny budget and it is doing that. It runs on donations, so far just mine. The bigger idea is that open-source software should be having its greatest era now that everyone has a DevOps genius at their fingertips. I chose to take a leap and build a platform to be part of that. Happy to answer questions. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50469853 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: Jigsaw - modern multiplayer jigsaw puzzles in the browser (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Our office removed the physical puzzle, so I built a multiplayer one. A coworker and I use it daily for a couple of hours. You can upload your own images and choose the number of pieces and the piece shape. Share the room link and others can join and solve with you in real time. There are a lot of keyboard shortcuts and power-user features. Stack: React, TypeScript, Vite, Node, WebSockets, SQLite, running on a Hetzner VPS. Pieces are rendered with WebGPU because it was fast and smooth. It works best on desktop but should be ok on mobile. I'd love some feedback!
